newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra eyes 18 uranium deposits - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra eyes 18 uranium deposits - paper.

text.p: The Australian government, which has ended limits on the number of uranium mines, had identified 18 major uranium deposits which could be exploited to cash in on booming world prices, The Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Thursday.
Canberra had earmarked four deposits which could speedily be developed into operating mines with A$625 million in investment, the paper said, quoting confidential government documents.

The four are the Northern Territory deposits of Jabiluka, owned by Energy Resources of Australia Ltd, and Koongarra, owned by Denison Mines Ltd and Cogema, and the Western Australian sites of Kintyre, owned by RTZ-CRA, and Yeelirrie, owned by WMC Ltd.
Australia's conservative Liberal-National govrnment axed the former Labor administration's three mine limit for the uranium industry after winning power in March.
Australia has about 29 percent of the world's known uranium reserves, but supplies only about 11 percent of the world market.
World prices have surged about 50 percent over the past year.
